claim: M1: a transient user service constrains four Node workers to aggregate one CPU worth of time, leaves all eight CPUs eligible, and disappears after a bounded four-second workload.
oracle: Actual service cpu.max=100000 100000, cpu.weight=25, nice=10, affinity0-7; nr_throttled increases and consumedCPU fits bounded elapsed time; service collected; unchanged desktop PID/private GPU mapping and no new GPU fault.

user_journey.scenario: Open Files and type while API Agents wait/run tools; interrupt/reconnect or manually adjust settings, then recover the desktop.
user_journey.expected: Desktop remains responsive and Agent processes retain progress; remote test alone cannot accept physical feel.

invariants: Observe cpu_capacity, compatible and cpufreq policy before choosing limits
Retain Linux scheduler access to all online cores for UI
Only task-owned transient background cgroup; no global affinity or IRQ writes
No sustained load while thermal telemetry unavailable
CPUQuota100% is aggregate one core time, not affinity or one physically reserved core
RuntimeMaxSec20s bounds failure; workload4s and four threads; no persistent files or global knobs
CPUWeight25 is relative only among sibling cgroups; does not prove fixed GUI priority ratio
gitnexus: Not applicable: standalone phone experiment outside neweval execution graph; inspect systemd command and actual cgroup files instead

unit.not_applicable_reason: No new reusable scheduler/launcher or parser is introduced. This experiment exercises existing systemd/Linux resource control with explicit runtime assertions; workload loops are not production logic. A reusable configurable launcher requires separate boundary tests.

faults: Enforced quota must show throttling under four workers
Normal unit collection; exit/failure status preserved

evidence: cpu-topology-observed.json: capacities160/498/1024; policy0/4/6 schedutil; EAS enabled; Node sees8
limitations: No thermal zones in prior inventory; avoid extended stress
CPU distribution cannot repair missing GPU, modem, WiFi or camera drivers
Node main event loop is single threaded; worker processes/threads and Go scheduler require workload-specific configuration
No background Harness production workload yet
exit_gate: Kernel cgroup files + Node worker execution + successful cleanup pass; this validates resource-control plumbing only, no default policy promotion or physical responsiveness claim.
